title: Huang Xing's three-kana telegrams, May 1916: the two telegrams of 20 May to Huang Xing (JACAR B03050089100, copy in B03050731100) and his reply of 25 May (B03050731500)

steps.what: JACAR B03050731500 fetched as PDF; telegram (frame 0246), cursive decode (0247), clerk's rendering (0248).
Romanised kana of frame 0246 transcribed: 139 kana in ten-letter words; decode on 0247 transcribed as 46 characters.
Three kana per character; consonant-row collisions 7 against 1.03 expected (p = 0.006), vowels at chance; read as row = digit, vowel free.
Alignment with the decode: dropping one kana at position 106 makes all repeated characters repeat as identical triples; deterministic three-kana code, 42 entries fixed. Free-vowel reading withdrawn.
All 3,628,800 row-to-digit permutations tested for a dictionary-order codebook (Spearman against telegraph-code order): best 0.524, null max 0.614.
Tomokiyo (Cryptiana) identifies the formula from the standard telegraph code to three kana, using this alignment; the dropped kana is a misread CHI (O HI).
saberwatchmanga/sun-circle-cipher-1916 identifies the 1916 print of the first 20 May telegram (護國軍紀事 no. 5) and audits the B03050089100 stream; no full reading.

Contributor (issue #48): both 20 May telegrams read with the formula: 133 groups as written, 86 after spelling corrections, 5 filled from the print, 4 inferred; telegram 1 matches the print 102/107; second copy found in B03050731100; reply re-decoded from Tomokiyo's romaji gives 詔 鬯 / 正寄函 / no 章.

Project: decoder written here from the formula alone (threekana.py) with the repository's own code table (sunyatsen/tw.csv); this project's 15 Sept transcription of the reply, with only the O HI -> CHI correction, decodes all 46 groups to 隱印崧詔鬯行諸兄鑒正寄函間適接哿電敬悉一切護國軍能速入湘贑甚好行嚴何日東渡望速啓行先電示興徑, the contributor's text exactly; the project's earlier 誥/蕘 邕 正發書 and 章 were misreadings of the cursive.

Project: all 219 coded groups of the contributor's final table decode under threekana.py and tw.csv to the contributor's character (219/219); telegram 1 against the print as transcribed by saberwatchmanga: 101 identical of 107 plus 刪/删 a variant form, so 102/107. The 86 spelling corrections themselves were not re-derived.

Project: B03050731100 fetched; images 24-26 are consul Ota's telegram no. 42 (Zhaoqing, 21 May 1916) forwarding the romaji stream at Cen Chunxuan's request, beginning sokahokaet arakotsuka atauichire as in B03050089100.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's three-kana formula (Sept 2026), identified on this correspondence, decodes the reply from this project's own transcription with one correction, and the two 20 May telegrams as contributed by Harumi-Matsuba.
outcome.fraction_read_source: reply_out.txt and sankana/groups.csv, unit kana triples: 46 + 103 + 117 = 266 of 275 groups decoded from the cipher (as written or after a spelling correction, end mark included); the 5 groups filled from the print and the 4 inferred counted as unread.

validation.notes: Key not recovered here (Tomokiyo's formula applied); Chinese plaintext, no letter model in lang/.

gaps.detail: Garbled in transmission (out-of-rule or transposed kana in both copies); filled from the 1916 print.

gaps.item: telegram 2, groups 164, 211, 223, 225 (贑, 出, 楷, 泰)
gaps.detail: Garbled groups (6381 has no character, out-of-rule or one kana off); inferred from context and the reply's addressees, grade I.

outcome.notes: Grades: H = read by the formula as written (reply 45, telegram 1 60, telegram 2 73, plus the end mark); M = read after a spelling correction (reply 1, telegram 1 43, telegram 2 43). 86 of 229 groups of the 20 May stream needed a spelling correction: in telegram 1 the print was in view, in telegram 2 there is no outside check beyond five spellings confirmed by the second copy. AI transcriptions only; no human check. Outside the LLM paper's scope (Chinese, not European classical).

credits.note: Three-kana formula (telegraph code -> three kana) and the O HI -> CHI correction; published the 1916 worksheet readings of the 20 May stream

Both 20 May 1916 telegrams read with the formula (229 groups, 86 spelling-corrected, 4 inferred), the second copy in B03050731100, the reply's addressees 詔 鬯 and 正寄函 from the cipher, the six senders identified
Showed that this project's cursive transcription of the reply (誥/蕘 邕, 正發書, 章行嚴) disagrees with the cipher
Found the 1916 print of telegram 1 (護國軍紀事 no. 5) and transcribed it; audit of the stream
The Japanese Foreign Ministry's 1916 decode of the reply (frame 0247)

prior.where: Reply: the Foreign Ministry's decode on frame 0247 (1916) and the print in 近代史資料 no. 50. Telegram 1: printed 1916 in 護國軍紀事 no. 5. Telegram 2: about 83 characters pencilled on the 1916 worksheets (published by Tomokiyo, Cryptiana chinesecrypto_e2.htm). Formula: Tomokiyo, 23 Sept 2026.

human: Reply: transcription and alignment by the project (Sept 2026). The 20 May telegrams were transcribed, corrected and read by Harumi-Matsuba with Claude and Codex (issue #48, 20 Oct 2026); the project re-ran the formula with its own decoder and code table and re-decoded the reply from its own transcription. No human checked any transcription letter by letter.
